title: Nelson Out Sunday, Week‑to‑Week: Knee Injury Sidelines Colts’ Star Guard 🚑🏈
body:
Seattle’s offensive line will be missing one of its newest pillars as left guard Quenton Nelson was ruled out for Sunday’s matchup with the Arizona Cardinals. The veteran interior lineman, who made his Seahawks debut only a week ago, has been placed on a week‑to‑week status after sustaining a knee injury in practice. The loss joins a growing list of absences for Seattle, as quarterback Sam Darnold and defensive end Leonard Williams have also been declared unavailable for the same contest.

Nelson’s arrival in Seattle was heralded as a significant upgrade to a line that struggled to protect quarterback Geno Smith last season. The three‑time All‑Pro, who spent the better part of a decade anchoring the Indianapolis Colts’ interior, signed a three‑year deal in the offseason with the expectation that his experience would stabilize the Seahawks’ run game and improve pass protection. In his first start against the New York Giants, Nelson helped the Seahawks rush for 124 yards and limited the opposition to just three sacks. Though the team fell short 17‑14, his presence was immediately felt, and his early performance suggested a quick return to form after a year spent on the Colts’ injured reserve list.

The timing of the injury is particularly problematic for Seattle’s offensive rhythm. With Darnold already sidelined, the Seahawks have been forced to rely on veteran backup quarterback Drew Locke, who has limited game‑time experience and is still acclimating to Smith’s cadence. The absence of a seasoned left guard could exacerbate protection issues, especially against a Cardinals front seven that features a strong pass rush led by rookie edge rusher J.J. Watt and veteran Chandler Jones. Analysts predict that Seattle may need to adjust its protection schemes, possibly shifting more responsibility to right guard Tyler Brockman and employing quick‑release passing concepts to mitigate pressure.

Defensively, the Seahawks also lose Leonard Williams, a versatile edge rusher who contributed 6.5 sacks last season. His injury further thins a unit already grappling with depth concerns after the loss of key contributors like Jarran Reed earlier in the year. The Cardinals, who have been on a winning streak, will look to exploit Seattle’s weakened trenches and press the Seahawks’ secondary with a balanced aerial attack. The matchup could become a test of Seattle’s depth, with special teams and backup players forced into larger roles than anticipated.

Head coach Pete Carroll addressed the situation in a brief press conference, emphasizing the “next‑man‑up” mentality that has defined his tenure. “We’re disappointed to lose Quenton so early in his Seattle career, but we have a group of guys ready to step in and do the work,” Carroll said. He also highlighted the importance of maintaining a clean pocket for Locke and trusting the run game to keep the defense honest. The coaching staff is expected to lean on veteran tight end Noah Fant for short-yardage protection and to incorporate more zone‑blocking schemes that can accommodate the shifting personnel.

Looking ahead, the Seahawks’ medical staff will continue to evaluate Nelson’s knee throughout the week, with the possibility of a return in the following game against the San Francisco 49ers. If the veteran lineman can recover quickly, Seattle’s offense could regain its footing before the crucial stretch run toward the playoffs. In the meantime, the team’s ability to adapt without several key starters will be a litmus test for its depth and resilience, and could shape the narrative of Seattle’s season as it battles for a postseason berth.
